# Gotchas

Incident-specific findings that aren't obvious from reading the code. Check this when working in the area a bullet names; it isn't meant to be read top-to-bottom every session (see `CONTRIBUTING.md` for standing rules that are).

- Also: register a new REST route's path in the `routes` output of `infra/terraform/modules/backend` (`PathPrefix`, priority) — only `/graphql` and `/beatrice-callbacks` are routed by default, so a new REST prefix is unreachable through the ingress until you add its own route.
- When bumping `BEATRICE_VERSION` in `.env`/`.env.example` (it picks the Beatrice image tag in `infra/terraform/local/1-app`), diff `smart-novel-beatrice`'s `src/utils/config.py` (or its `docs/schema.graphql`) between the old and new tag before assuming the environment in `infra/terraform/modules/beatrice` still works — Beatrice has repeatedly shipped a breaking config/contract change on a minor bump with no migration note. All surfaced as the `beatrice` pod crash-looping on `task dev:start`, not as a compile-time or unit-test failure.
- Beatrice's `generateAudio` needs `TTS__BASE_URL` pointed at an OpenAI-compatible speech endpoint (the real provider in `.env`, or WireMock in e2e) (5.0.0+ requires `TTS__BASE_URL`, `TTS__API_KEY`, `TTS__MODEL`, `TTS__VOICES`, with no defaults) — without it every `generateAudio` call fails. Not obvious from the error alone; found only by checking Beatrice's own logs during a live `generateAudio` call.
- When a `REQUIREMENTS.md` step's prose describes a new component (e.g. "a small bridge service") that would duplicate a subscription/connection/map lookup an earlier step already set up, treat that as a description of the _behavior_ to add, not a literal instruction to create a new class — extend the existing owner instead, unless there's a real reason (different lifecycle, different failure domain) to split it out. Surfaced in Step 2.2: the AC described a "bridge service" for re-publishing Redis status updates onto GraphQL `PubSub`, but `ChapterNarrationService` (Step 2.1) already subscribed to that same channel and held the job-to-chapter map; a second subscription would have duplicated both for no benefit.
- This environment's own memory-pressure monitor kills a long `task dev:start`/`task backend-e2e:run` invocation well before real host memory is exhausted — recurred across multiple full `backend-e2e` runs, including once right at the very end after `openai-compatible-tts`'s real synthesis (`python3 server.py`) had grown to several GB RSS, with `free -h` showing tens of GB still available at the moment of the kill. Deliberately passing `run_in_background: true` up front gets killed far more reliably than a plain foreground call the tool auto-backgrounds after its own ~600s cap once already running — prefer the latter. Either way, check the partial log before assuming a killed run failed outright: vitest prints each passed/failed test as it goes, so a kill after the last `✓`/`×` line still tells you the real per-test outcome.
- Real TTS synthesis against the CPU-only local shim under several tests' concurrent load produces polling-timeout failures that move between different tests on each rerun, never the same test twice, and never on incorrect output — that pattern is resource contention, not a regression; confirm by rerunning 2-3 times and, if still unsure, cross-check with an isolated graphql-api-tester call against the dev server.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` step prose can get a route path wrong even for a brand-new route (not just when changing an existing one) — it's written before the step is built, so it can guess a scheme that doesn't match the app's actual router. Step 3 (Create Chapter) said `/novels/:novelId/chapters/new`, but `apps/frontend/src/app/app.tsx`'s actual novel routes are all singular, `/novel/:id/...` (`ChapterEditPage`, `ChapterReadPage`, etc. all navigate via `` `/novel/${novel.id}/...` ``). Always check the real router file before wiring a new route, and follow its established scheme over the requirements doc's literal path when they disagree — the AC is the outcome (a working create page), not the exact URL string.
- This repo's Storybook-only mocks for `generated/graphql.ts` work via a custom Vite plugin in `.storybook/main.ts` that swaps the import per **importer file path** (see `mockGeneratedGraphql`) — this only applies inside Storybook's own Vite build, not under plain `vitest`. To exercise a story's `play` function as a build-time proxy when no browser tool is available (per the entry below on Storybook verification), a temporary spec must `vi.mock('../../generated/graphql', ...)` and delegate the mocked hook to the _same_ mock module the story's decorators mutate (e.g. `chapter-create-page.mock.ts`'s `mockCreateChapterMutationState`) — mocking generated/graphql some other way in the temp spec makes the story's own decorators silently no-op, since they're mutating a mock object the component never actually reads under vitest.
- A Kubernetes Service named like a component injects `<NAME>_PORT=tcp://<ip>:<port>` (and related) variables into every pod of the namespace. Pods whose image or application reads its own `<NAME>_PORT` (`backend`, `frontend`) must set `enable_service_links = false`, or they crash or read the wrong port. Surfaced running the former LLM gateway on kind.
- Beatrice does not reconnect when RabbitMQ is unreachable at startup (the connection stays closed and the queue has no consumer), so `modules/app` makes it wait for RabbitMQ and the AI components. A `Running` Beatrice pod is not proof; check `rabbitmqctl list_queues name consumers` shows a consumer.
- Changing the `kind_cluster` definition (for example adding a port mapping) makes Terraform want to replace the cluster, and `terraform destroy` then fails refreshing resources on a cluster whose provider is unknown. `task dev:stop` falls back to `kind delete cluster` and drops the state; run it on the old definition before changing it.
- Fithara's own rate limit is per client, and every request reaches it from the backend's one address, so it is shared by all users. The per-user limit lives in the backend (`MAX_TURNS_PER_USER_PER_HOUR`, counted from stored turns).
- ent (Go backend): an entity returned by a query inside a transaction keeps that transaction's connection, so loading one of its edges (a GraphQL field such as `Novel.tags`) after the commit fails with "transaction has already been committed or rolled back". Commit, then read the row again with the plain client (`novel.Service.Create` does).
- entgql (Go backend): a cursor on a nullable order column (`first_chapter_created_at`) falls back to the ID alone when the value is NULL, so paging loses its place at the border between rows with and without a value, and PostgreSQL puts NULLs first when descending. `novel.PageByFirstChapter` is the hand-written keyset; any new nullable `entgql.OrderField` needs the same.
- entgql (Go backend): `QueryField` and every edge publish the entity they point to with all its columns. `Novel.writer: Writer!` would have handed out every writer's email. After adding a `QueryField`, an edge or a field, read the diff of `apps/backend/api/ent.graphql` (git-ignored: run `task backend:generate` and read the file) and `entgql.Skip` what must stay private.
- gqlgen (Go backend): an enum argument that arrives as a copy is not the package-level pointer (`orderBy.Field == ent.NovelOrderFieldFirstChapterCreatedAt` is always false, because `UnmarshalGQL` copies the struct); compare `Field.String()`.
- ent `sql.Builder.Ident("a.b")` quotes the dot as part of the name; write the table, the dot and the column separately when a predicate reaches into another table.
- `backend-e2e` against a stack you started yourself (`task dev:start`): `vitest.config.ts` with `globalSetup: []` through `mergeConfig` still runs the cluster setup, because arrays are concatenated; spread the base config and set `test.globalSetup` instead (as `PROCESS.md` says), and delete the throwaway file afterwards.
